## Incident Report — MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### 1. Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 10.11.26.183 |
| MAC address | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (NetBIOS names DESKTOP-B8TQK49 and NEMOTODES also broadcast from this IP via NBNS) |
| AD domain | nemotoads.health (Kerberos realm NEMOTODES.HEALTH, DC 10.11.26.3 = NEMOTODE-DC) |
| Logged-in Windows user | oboomwald (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, both against the local realm and against NEMOTODES.HEALTH) |

### 2. Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution basis: signature-confirmed, corroborated by protocol inspection.** Suricata fired multiple ETPRO/ET signatures naming NetSupport directly against 10.11.26.183 <-> 194.180.191.64 (`ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`). I independently verified this in the pcap:
- HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every POST to 194.180.191.64.
- POST bodies use the literal NetSupport client protocol: `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1\n` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<encrypted blob>\n`.
- A GET to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` (104.26.1.231) immediately preceded C2 check-in — this is NetSupport's own vendor geolocation endpoint, queried by the client at startup.

### 3. Infection Chain (observed in traffic)
1. 08:50:11–08:50:16 (capture-local time, UTC+4): browsing redirect chain `classicgrand.com` → `confirmsubscription.com` → `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) — a scam/cracked-software lure page. Also flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup/TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk.com)`.
2. Four separate large TLS sessions to 193.42.38.139:443 followed (up to 5.7 MB transferred in one session), consistent with the RAT client/installer being pulled down over HTTPS. Content is TLS-encrypted, so no filename or SHA256 could be recovered from the wire.
3. 08:50:45: victim immediately performs the NetSupport geolocation lookup and begins C2 check-ins to 194.180.191.64 — establishing the RAT was installed and launched at this point.
4. From 08:50:45 through the end of the capture (09:43), the host beacons to the C2 roughly every 60 seconds via HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, continuing for the full ~48-minute remaining capture window.

Note: EFSR/SMBv1/NTLMSSP-overflow alerts at 04:49:38–04:50:10 UTC target 10.11.26.3 (the DC) from 10.11.26.183 and predate the malvertising chain by roughly an hour; these look like routine (if legacy/insecure) domain-join SMB/RPC chatter rather than RAT-driven lateral movement, and are not tied to any NetSupport indicator.

### 4. Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- 194.180.191.64:443 (plain HTTP masquerading on port 443 — flagged by Suricata as `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443`)
  - URI: `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`
  - User-Agent: `NetSupport Manager/1.3`
  - Beacon interval: ~60 seconds

**Malicious/lure domains**
- modandcrackedapk.com → 193.42.38.139 (delivery site for the RAT payload, TLS)
- classicgrand.com → 213.246.109.5 (upstream redirector in the lure chain)
- confirmsubscription.com → 13.56.30.207 / 52.8.34.0 (upstream redirector in the lure chain)

**Malware-associated infrastructure (vendor domain, abused by the RAT client)**
- geo.netsupportsoftware.com → 104.26.1.231, GET `/location/loca.asp`

**File names / hashes**
None recoverable. The payload delivery from modandcrackedapk.com occurred entirely inside TLS sessions, so no filename, Content-Disposition header, or file hash is visible in the capture. No cleartext executable transfer or file hash was observed anywhere else in the traffic. State plainly: no SHA256 can be reported for the dropped binary from this pcap alone.

### 5. Recommended Actions
- Isolate 10.11.26.183 (DESKTOP-B8TQK49, user oboomwald) from the network immediately.
- Block 194.180.191.64, 193.42.38.139, classicgrand.com, confirmsubscription.com, modandcrackedapk.com at the perimeter/DNS.
- Image the host and pull the actual NetSupport client binary/config from disk (typically under `%ProgramFiles%\NetSupport\NetSupport Manager\client32.exe` or similar) to obtain a hash and confirm the config points at 194.180.191.64.
- Force credential reset for oboomwald given confirmed remote-access-tool presence on the account's session.
